message: No detected untrusted source handling: Data is loaded from a local directory (fetch_data reads local JSON files) with no checksum verification, signature validation, or authenticated source handling.
No detected label flipping detection: No code inspects or validates label distributions, checks label values against an expected set, or uses any label-noise detection tool before training.

No detected data poisoning defenses: The data preparation path (fetch_data, fetch_ts, engineer_features) only checks for directory existence and correct column names; there is no outlier detection, statistical anomaly checking, or filtering of suspicious training samples.

No detected model integrity verification: The model_load function loads serialized joblib files from a local directory using joblib.load without any hash check, signature verification, or pinned revision validation.
No detected label distribution validation: No code checks class balance, expected label sets, or anomalous label distributions before or during training.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no trigger detection, activation analysis, or gradient anomaly detection implemented anywhere in the training pipeline.
No detected differential privacy: No differential privacy libraries or mechanisms (e.g., Opacus, TF Privacy, DP-SGD) are imported or applied during training.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness testing frameworks (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD, etc.) or any robustness stress tests are present anywhere in the code.

No detected metric tampering protection: Although a train-test split is performed, the model is then retrained on all data before saving, there is no held-out isolated test set, no signing/hashing of evaluation data, and only a single metric (RMSE) is logged without any integrity protection.

No detected output bounds checks: The inference path only converts numpy arrays to lists for JSON serialization but performs no NaN guards, probability bounds checks, or sanity validation on model outputs before returning them.
No detected prompt injection defenses: This is a time-series regression model (RandomForestRegressor), not an LLM, so prompt-injection defenses are not applicable and none are implemented.
